verses.1: When he opened the seventh seal, there came silence in heaven for about half an hour.
verses.2: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and they were given seven trumpets.
verses.3: Another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a golden censer, and he was given much incense to offer with the prayers of the saints on the golden altar before the throne.
verses.4: And the smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God from the hand of the angel.
verses.5: Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it to the earth, and there came thunder and voices and lightning and an earthquake.
verses.6: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.
verses.7: The first sounded, and there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and they were thrown to the earth; and a third of the earth burned, and a third of the trees burned, and all the green grass burned.
verses.8: The second angel sounded, and something like a great mountain on fire was thrown into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood,
verses.9: and a third of the creatures in the sea that had life died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
verses.10: The third angel sounded, and a great star like a torch fell from the sky, burning, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
verses.11: The name of the star is called *Apsinthos*. And a third of the waters became bitter, like apsinth, and many people died from the waters, because they were poisoned.
verses.12: The fourth angel sounded, and a third of the sun was struck, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them were darkened, and the day lost a third of its light, and the night similarly.
verses.13: And I saw and heard a bird flying in midheaven crying with a loud voice: "Woe! Woe! Woe! To those who live on the earth from the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels still to sound."

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: "half an hour" is a symbolic measure of time in apocalyptic literature.  
- v. 11: "Apsinthos" is the Greek name of the herb rue; the term is retained as a transliteration, given its specific symbolic meaning.  
- v. 13: "midheaven" is a rendering of *mesouranēma*, meaning "mid-sky" or "midheavens."

[1] When he opened the seventh seal, there came silence in heaven for about half an hour.  
[2] And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and they were given seven trumpets.  
[3] Another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a golden censer, and he was given much incense to offer with the prayers of the saints on the golden altar before the throne.  
[4] And the smoke of the incense, with the prayers of the saints, went up before God from the hand of the angel.  
[5] Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it to the earth, and there came thunder and voices and lightning and an earthquake.  
[6] And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.  
[7] The first sounded, and there came hail and fire mixed with blood, and they were thrown to the earth; and a third of the earth burned, and a third of the trees burned, and all the green grass burned.  
[8] The second angel sounded, and something like a great mountain on fire was thrown into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood,  
[9] and a third of the creatures in the sea that had life died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.  
[10] The third angel sounded, and a great star like a torch fell from the sky, burning, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.  
[11] The name of the star is called *Apsinthos*. And a third of the waters became bitter, like apsinth, and many people died from the waters, because they were poisoned.  
[12] The fourth angel sounded, and a third of the sun was struck, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them were darkened, and the day lost a third of its light, and the night similarly.  
[13] And I saw and heard a bird flying in midheaven crying with a loud voice: "Woe! Woe! Woe! To those who live on the earth from the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels still to sound."

Notes  
- v. 1: "half an hour" is a symbolic measure of time in apocalyptic literature.  
- v. 11: "Apsinthos" is the Greek name of the herb rue; the term is retained as a transliteration, given its specific symbolic meaning.  
- v. 13: "midheaven" is a rendering of *mesouranēma*, meaning "mid-sky" or "midheavens."
